# HR — Employees, Leave, Attendance, Payroll, Shifts

## What it does

HR runs the people side of the business: who works here, when they are
off, whether they showed up, and what they are paid. An **Employee** gets
leave allocated, applies for it, is marked present or absent, works a
**Shift**, and is paid through a **Salary Slip** generated by a **Payroll
Entry**. In v16 the HR module is the separate **Frappe HR** app (hrms) —
the Employee master itself still sits in ERPNext core, and HRMS builds on
it.

## Core DocTypes

| DocType | What it is |
|---|---|
| Employee | The master: name, company, department, designation, date of joining, reports-to. |
| Leave Type | A kind of leave: Annual, Sick, Casual — with its rules. |
| Leave Allocation | Grants leave days to an employee for a period. |
| Leave Application | The request: dates, leave type, approver. Posts to the leave ledger on submit. |
| Leave Ledger Entry | One leave movement. Created automatically — **never insert it by hand**. |
| Attendance | One day's record: Present, Absent, Half Day, On Leave. |
| Employee Checkin | One punch: in or out, with time (from biometric or manual entry). |
| Shift Type | A shift: start, end, late-entry and early-exit rules. |
| Shift Assignment | Puts an employee on a shift for a period. |
| Holiday List | The year's holidays, per company or location. |
| Salary Structure | The pay design: earnings and deductions (basic, allowances, tax, provident fund). |
| Salary Structure Assignment | Assigns a structure to an employee from a date. |
| Salary Slip | One month's pay for one employee: gross, deductions, net. |
| Payroll Entry | The payroll run: generates Salary Slips for a set of employees. |
| Expense Claim | An employee's claim (travel, fuel) for approval and payment. |

## End-to-end flow

```text
Setup:   Departments → Holiday List → Leave Types → Shift Types → Salary Structures
Hire:    Employee → Leave Allocation → Shift Assignment → Salary Structure Assignment
Daily:   Employee Checkin → Attendance (auto-marked from checkins)
Leave:   Leave Application (submit) → balance drops → Attendance shows On Leave
Pay:     Payroll Entry → Salary Slips → Payment Entry (bank) → ledger
Check:   Leave Balance, Attendance, Salary Register reports
```

- **Leave Allocation** grants the days; **Leave Application** spends
  them. No allocation, no application — the balance goes negative and the
  report shows it.
- **Attendance** can be marked from **Employee Checkin** (biometric or
  manual punches) or entered directly. Checkins are the audit trail;
  attendance is the record payroll reads.
- **Payroll Entry** is the run: pick the period and the employees, and it
  generates the Salary Slips. A slip is per employee per month — never
  edit a submitted slip, cancel and regenerate it.
- **Salary Structure** is where the pay policy lives: basic pay, house
  rent, medical, tax and provident fund as components. Change the policy
  in the structure, not in individual slips.

## Worked example — a factory, one month

A spice factory has 45 staff on two shifts:

1. **Employees** created with department, designation and joining date.
   **Holiday List** for the year, **Shift Types** Morning (8–4) and Evening
   (4–12), **Shift Assignments** per worker.
2. Daily, workers punch in. **Employee Checkin** records feed
   **Attendance** — Present, Late, or Absent.
3. A worker applies for 3 days annual leave. **Leave Application**
   approved; balance drops from 12 to 9; those days show On Leave.
4. Month end: **Payroll Entry** generates 45 **Salary Slips**. Late days
   deduct per the salary structure; leave days are paid. Slips are
   submitted and paid by bank in one **Payment Entry**.
5. The **Salary Register** shows gross, deductions and net per employee —
   the same report the accountant files with.

## A real use case

A 60-person company ran attendance in a register and payroll in Excel.
Leave balances lived in the HR head's memory, and salary day took three
days of rechecking. After HR, checkins mark attendance automatically,
leave balances are visible to everyone, and the payroll run takes an
afternoon — with the Salary Register as the audit record.

**How we can use it:** sell HR as the second module after Accounting for
any client with 20+ staff — attendance + leave + payroll is the package
every growing business feels the pain of. Biometric checkin sync is a
small fixed-price add-on (see the apps catalog's HR entries).

## Common mistakes

- **Leave without allocation.** Applications against zero balance create
  negative balances and arguments at year end.
- **Payroll from edited slips.** A submitted Salary Slip is a record —
  cancel and regenerate, never edit.
- **No Shift Assignment.** Without it, checkins have nothing to compare
  against and "late" has no meaning.
- **Salary policy in slips, not structures.** The same allowance typed
  into 45 slips is 45 chances to be wrong. Put it in the structure.
- **Attendance marked by hand daily.** Use checkins. Manual attendance for
  45 people is a full-time job and a source of disputes.
